subject: English
passage:
The following text is adapted from Charlotte Brontë's 1847 novel Jane Eyre. The speaker, Edward, is explaining his decision to host a modest dinner party for a small circle of friends.

I intend nothing more than a quiet evening of refined conversation among those whose society I value. We seek no grand entertainment or fashionable display. I have every confidence that our gathering will be conducted with perfect propriety; and I believe there can be no impropriety in offering our guests the simple hospitality of our own table rather than attempting some elaborate spectacle beyond our means.
prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To reveal that Edward has changed his approach to entertaining from his previous practices
choices.B: To suggest that Edward and his household lack the resources to organize a sophisticated social event
choices.C: To provide Edward's assurance that the dinner will be appropriate and involve only a close circle of acquaintances
choices.D: To indicate that Edward plans to make the dinner party an elaborate public occasion

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer because it most accurately portrays the main purpose of the text. At the beginning of the text, Edward states that he intends "nothing more than a quiet evening" among those whose "society I value," emphasizing the limited and selective nature of the gathering. Then, Edward assures that the gathering will be conducted with "perfect propriety," and he further justifies that offering "simple hospitality" is more appropriate than attempting "some elaborate spectacle beyond our means." Overall, the main purpose of the text is to convey Edward's promise that the dinner will be appropriate and involve only a close circle.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect. Although Edward mentions avoiding "elaborate spectacle beyond our means," he frames this as a matter of appropriateness rather than addressing any general lack of resources or sophistication in his household.
